source.author: verg
source.text: Est lucos Silari circa ilicibusque; virentem plurimus Alburnum volitans, cui nomen asilo Romanum est, oestrum Grai vertere vocantes, asper, acerba sonans, quo tota exterrita silvis diffugiunt armenta; furit mugitibus aether concussus silvaeque et sicci ripa Tanagri.
source.text_original: Est lucos Silari circa ilicibusque; virentem / plurimus Alburnum volitans, cui nomen asilo / Romanum est, oestrum Grai vertere vocantes, / asper, acerba sonans, quo tota exterrita silvis / diffugiunt armenta; furit mugitibus aether / concussus silvaeque et sicci ripa Tanagri.
source.text_english: There are groves around Silarus and oaks; very often, buzzing around the green Alburnus, there is an insect to which the Roman name is asilus, and the Greeks, calling it oestrus, have translated it; rough, with a harsh sound, at which the whole herd, terrified, scatters through the woods; the air rages, shaken by their lowings, and the woods and the bank of dry Tanagrus.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Cui nomen asilo, Romanum est: oestrum Graii vertere vocantes, Asper acerba sonans: quo tota exterrita silvis Diffugiunt armenta: furit mugitibus aether Concussus, silvaeque et sicci ripa Tanagri.
reuse.text_original: Cui nomen asilo, Romanum est: oestrum Graii vertere vocantes, Asper acerba sonans: quo tota exterrita silvis Diffugiunt armenta: furit mugitibus aether Concussus, silvaeque et sicci ripa Tanagri.
reuse.text_english: Its name is asilus; this is the Roman term. The Greeks, who call it oestrus, render it Asper, sounding harshly bitter. At its attack the whole herd, terrified, scatters through the woods; the air roars, shaken by lowing, and so do the forests and the bank of the dry Tanagris.
